scope: Proposition 6.4 (Density of qualified pins) of the manuscript “Cardy’s formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation” (preprints/Cardys-formula-for-critical-Poisson-Voronoi-percolation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 224 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1334302b31272ae0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 46-47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist a finite normalized menu and fixed β, β′ > 0 such that the following holds in every bulk patch with B(x, 6R) available. With probability 46 tending to one in the ordered limit ε → 0, then h → 0, every subarc of diameter at least rh in B(x, 2R) on a rim reaching outside B(x, 4R) contains a qualified pin. The statement holds simultaneously for all such subarcs and both colors. It also holds for the coupled bulk settings on their patch-agreement event.
